target_customer: Airports, retailers and commercial real estate operators that pay to turn existing cameras into occupancy and operations data
problem: Operators of physical spaces lack real time data on queues and crowds; dedicated sensors are costly, so Zensors turns existing cameras into sensors.
business_model: B2B software subscription for visual AI

founders.name: Anuraag Jain
founders.role: CEO (company page: Head of Product and Technology)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder with no bio. CMU pages credit him as the technology creator and tie the company to research at Carnegie Mellon.

founders.name: Chris Harrison
founders.role: Founder (Director of the Future Interfaces Group at Carnegie Mellon)
founders.background_notes: Zensors company about page lists him as a founder beside Anuraag Jain; it cites Forbes 30 under 30 science and MIT Technology Review 35 under 35 recognition.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable video understanding across arbitrary camera feeds and privacy preserving deployment was research heavy in 2019 to 2021, originating in CMU HCI research.

defensibility.rationale: Airport and enterprise deployments and the CMU research base create some barrier, but camera analytics vendors were many.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying was found; the company still sells to airports as of its own site.

market_need_then: COVID-19 in 2020 raised demand for crowd and occupancy monitoring; CMU reported Zensors used against COVID in April 2020 and an early installation at Pittsburgh International Airport estimated security wait times in 2019.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself; recognition rests on CMU origin and airport customers. The name is easy to confuse with Zensors-like sensor names.

outcome_analysis: Zensors grew out of Carnegie Mellon research and reached airport customers, later repositioning as physical AI with a 12 person team. Sources show only very small seed amounts and no priced institutional round, so the funding history is uncertain. It remains active and selling to airports, retailers and ExxonMobil per its site, but the funding picture is too thin to explain its stage.
notes: Funding is unverified: aggregators report about 125K to 160K USD total across small seed rounds (CB Insights lists 11 rounds, a 0.13M seed dated 2021-08-30), so none were recorded as rounds. Chris Harrison is now listed as a founder because the Zensors about page names him as one of two founders. Competitor search returned only current-era listings (VergeSense, Density), not sources dated at the 2021 batch, so the list is empty. Sources disagree on founding year (2018 or 2019) and headquarters. Completeness pass: a 0.13M seed dated 2021-08-30 is recorded from CB Insights alone, a single database; the CB Insights total is about 160K across 11 rounds and a search snippet dates its latest seed to 2022-09, so the history is incomplete and sources conflict.
